examples.en: I'm learning Vietnamese.
Please teach me how to greet someone in Vietnamese.
My friend is good at both Korean and Vietnamese.
Vietnamese has tones, so it's difficult.
This menu also has Vietnamese descriptions.
We are looking for a Vietnamese interpreter.

explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 '-어'를 붙이면 그 나라 언어가 돼요. 한국어, 일본어, 중국어처럼요. '베트남 말'이라고 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요.

phrases.example: 베트남 말을 조금 할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: I can speak a little Vietnamese.
phrases.nuance_ko: '베트남어'를 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out way of saying 베트남어.

phrases.en: My friend spoke in Vietnamese, so I couldn't understand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 언어로 말하는지 '-로'로 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -로 to say which language is spoken.

phrases.en: There is a Vietnamese class every Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언어 이름 뒤에 '수업'을 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 수업 after a language name for a class.

explain_en: Adding '-어' after a country name gives its language, as in 한국어, 일본어 and 중국어. You can also say it more loosely as '베트남 말'.

examples.en: I'm studying Arabic at university.
Arabic is written from right to left.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 아랍어로 불러서 뜻을 몰라요.
examples.en: This song is sung in Arabic, so I don't know the meaning.

examples.ko: 친구가 아랍어를 잘해서 도움을 많이 받았어요.
examples.en: My friend is good at Arabic, so I got a lot of help.

examples.ko: 아랍어 수업은 매주 화요일 저녁에 있어요.
examples.en: The Arabic class is every Tuesday evening.
I bought an Arabic book because I'm going to Egypt.

explain: 아랍어는 글을 오른쪽에서 왼쪽으로 쓰는 언어예요. '아랍어를 배우다/하다/잘하다'처럼 써요. 나라마다 말투가 많이 달라서 '아랍어 방언'이라는 말도 자주 해요.

phrases.en: My friend is very good at Arabic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언어 실력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about language skill.

phrases.en: Arabic dialects are different in each country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라마다 다른 말투를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the different speech styles of each country.

phrases.en: I tried greeting in Arabic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 언어를 사용하는지 말할 때 '-로'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-ro' shows which language is being used.

explain_en: Arabic is written from right to left. Say 아랍어를 배우다/하다/잘하다. Speech differs a lot from country to country, so people often talk about 아랍어 방언 (Arabic dialects).

examples.en: I'm learning Italian because of cooking.
Italian sounds soft like a song.
The restaurant menu was written only in Italian.
Our Italian teacher came from Rome.

examples.ko: 여행 가기 전에 이탈리아어 인사를 외웠어요.
examples.en: Before the trip I memorized some Italian greetings.

examples.ko: 이탈리아어를 조금만 해도 현지 사람들이 좋아해요.
examples.en: Even a little Italian makes the locals happy.

explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 '어'를 붙인 언어 이름이에요(이탈리아+어). 줄여서 '이태리어'라고 하는 분도 있는데 지금은 '이탈리아어'가 표준이에요. 한국에서는 음식 이름 때문에 이탈리아어 단어를 접할 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: I want to learn Italian.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언어를 배운다고 할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb for learning a language.

phrases.example: 이탈리아어 단어를 하루에 다섯 개씩 외워요.
phrases.en: I memorize five Italian words a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이탈리아어의 낱말을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to individual Italian words.

phrases.en: My Italian teacher is really fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이탈리아어를 가르치는 선생님이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A teacher who teaches Italian.

explain_en: A language name made of the country name + 어 (이탈리아 + 어). Some older speakers say 이태리어, but 이탈리아어 is the standard now. Koreans meet Italian words often through food names.

en: to go for a drive (for pleasure)

examples.en: I sometimes go for a drive to the sea on weekends.
I went for a drive to the Han River with a friend at night.
If the weather is nice, I want to go for a drive.
I listened to songs during the drive.
Do you want to go for a drive together this weekend?
I opened the window and felt the wind while driving around.

explain: '드라이브'는 목적지 없이 즐기려고 차를 타고 다니는 일이에요. 출퇴근처럼 일 때문에 운전하면 '운전하다'라고 해요. 영어 drive와 달리 'drive a car'는 '드라이브'가 아니라 '운전하다'예요.

phrases.en: The weather was nice, so I went for a drive with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '드라이브하다'보다 '가다'를 써서 어디론가 나가는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using 가다 gives more of a feeling of heading out somewhere.

phrases.en: On the weekend I go for a drive to the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)러 가다'로 드라이브가 목적이라는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -(으)러 가다 to show that driving is the purpose of the trip.

phrases.en: When the rain stops, I want to go for a drive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바라는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 싶다 expresses a wish.
phrases.en_equiv: to want to go for a drive

explain_en: '드라이브' is riding around in a car for fun, often with no set destination. Driving for work or commuting is '운전하다'. Unlike English, 'drive a car' is '운전하다', not '드라이브하다'.

examples.ko: 이 노트북은 영상 편집도 문제없이 돼요.
examples.en: This laptop can handle video editing without any problem.
The exam ended without any problems.
The service runs smoothly even when the number of users grows.
The plane arrived on time without any trouble.

examples.ko: 그 일은 저 혼자서도 문제없이 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can do that job on my own without any trouble.
The app installed on my phone without any problem.

explain: '문제없이 되다', '문제없이 돌아가다', '문제없이 끝나다'처럼 일이 막힘없이 진행될 때 써요. '무사히'는 위험한 일을 지나서 안전하게라는 느낌이 강하고, '문제없이'는 오류나 불편이 없다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The machine runs without any problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 시스템이 잘 작동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a machine or system works well.

phrases.en: I arrived without any problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아무'를 붙이면 문제가 전혀 없었다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 아무 strongly says there was no problem at all.

phrases.example: 이 앱은 문제없이 사용할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can use this app without any problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 앱을 불편 없이 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say it when you can use a thing or app without trouble.

explain_en: Use it when things proceed smoothly, as in '문제없이 되다', '문제없이 돌아가다' or '문제없이 끝나다'. '무사히' leans toward getting through something risky safely, while '문제없이' means no errors or trouble.

examples.en: I always take a water bottle when I work out.

examples.ko: 나가기 전에 물통에 물을 가득 채웠어요.
examples.en: Before leaving, I filled the water bottle to the top.

examples.ko: 제 물통은 작고 파란색이라서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: My water bottle is small and blue, so it stands out.

examples.ko: 가방 옆 주머니에 물통이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: There is a water bottle in the side pocket of the bag.
The water bottle lid doesn't close well.

examples.ko: 학교에 갈 때 물통을 두고 와서 후회했어요.
examples.en: I left my water bottle behind when I went to school and regretted it.

explain: '물통'은 운동·등산·학교에 들고 다니는 튼튼한 통을 말할 때 자주 써요. 식탁이나 냉장고에 두는 병은 '물병', 보온이 되는 컵은 '텀블러'라고 구분해서 말해요. 물을 사 마실 때는 '생수'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I packed my water bottle for the picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나갈 때 가방에 넣는 물건이라서 '챙기다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is something you put in your bag, so it goes well with 챙기다 (to pack).

phrases.example: 산에 갈 때는 큰 물통이 필요해요.
phrases.en: You need a big water bottle when you go hiking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 말할 때 앞에 형용사를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an adjective in front to describe the size.

phrases.en: I can't open the lid of my water bottle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물통의 부분을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for talking about a part of the bottle.

explain_en: 물통 is the usual word for a sturdy container you carry to exercise, hiking, or school. A bottle kept on the table or in the fridge is a 물병, and an insulated cup is a 텀블러. Water you buy to drink is called 생수.

examples.en: Freestyle is the easiest in swimming.

examples.ko: 저는 자유형으로 백 미터를 헤엄칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can swim a hundred meters freestyle.
After learning freestyle, I learned backstroke too.
I watched the freestyle final at the Olympics.
In freestyle, the timing of your breathing matters.

examples.ko: 오늘 수영 시간에 자유형 발차기를 연습했어요.
examples.en: In swim class today we practiced the freestyle kick.

explain: 수영 종목으로 '평영, 배영, 접영'과 같이 나와요. 어떤 방법으로 헤엄쳐도 되는 종목이라 '자유형'이지만 보통은 팔을 번갈아 돌리는 영법을 해요. '자유형 100미터'처럼 거리와 함께 말해요.

phrases.en: I swim the 100-meter freestyle in under a minute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종목 이름 뒤에 거리를 붙여서 경기나 기록을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the distance after the event name when talking about a race or a time.

phrases.example: 저는 자유형으로 헤엄치는 것을 제일 좋아해요.
phrases.en: I like swimming freestyle the most.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 어떤 영법으로 수영하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '으로' tells which stroke you swim with.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is a freestyle swimmer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자유형 경기에 나가는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a person who competes in freestyle events.

explain_en: It appears alongside '평영' (breaststroke), '배영' (backstroke), and '접영' (butterfly) as a swimming event. Any stroke is allowed, hence the name, but swimmers normally alternate their arms. People say it with the distance, such as '자유형 100미터'.

examples.en: I meet my friend at the metro station.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 전철역과 가까워서 출근하기 편해요.
examples.en: My home is close to the metro station, so commuting is easy.
There are lots of good restaurants near the metro station.
Where is the nearest metro station?
It rained, so I took a taxi to the metro station.
The metro station has so many exits that I get confused.

explain: '지하철역'이라고도 하고, 약속 장소를 말할 때는 '○○역'이라고만 해도 돼요. '전철역 근처', '전철역 출구'처럼 길 찾기나 집 위치를 설명할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: There is a subway station near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 다른 말이에요. 둘 다 일상에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A synonym; both are common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: There are many good restaurants near the metro station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 가게의 위치를 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe where a home or shop is.

phrases.en: Let's meet at exit 3 of the metro station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 정할 때 번호와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said with a number when setting a meeting spot.

explain_en: People also say '지하철역', and when naming a meeting place, just '○○역' is enough. It comes up in giving directions or describing where a home is, such as '전철역 근처' (near the station) or '전철역 출구' (station exit).

examples.en: At the movie theater, popcorn is a must.
One large popcorn, please.
I made popcorn myself at home in the microwave.

examples.ko: 냄비에서 팝콘이 튀는 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the popcorn popping loudly in the pot.

examples.ko: 저는 달콤한 맛보다 짭짤한 팝콘이 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer salty popcorn to sweet.
I spilled the popcorn and the floor became a mess.

explain: 한국 영화관에서는 팝콘과 음료를 세트로 많이 팔고, 맛은 오리지널·캐러멜·치즈 중에서 골라요. 영화 볼 때 먹는 대표 간식이라서 '팝콘 먹으면서 영화 보자'라는 말을 자주 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a tub of popcorn at the movie theater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팝콘의 양을 말할 때 '통'으로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Popcorn is counted with the word 통 (tub/container).

phrases.en: I watched a movie while eating popcorn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팝콘과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common verb used with popcorn.

phrases.en: I like caramel popcorn the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팝콘 앞에 맛 이름을 붙여서 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a flavor name before the word to say which kind of popcorn.

explain_en: Korean movie theaters often sell popcorn and a drink as a set, and you choose a flavor such as original, caramel, or cheese. It is the classic movie snack, so people often say '팝콘 먹으면서 영화 보자' (let's watch a movie with popcorn).
